action_summary: The owner asked whether instant learning in new arbitrary environments is already solved. Every number in the tree that says so was measured on environments written in the tree. This action measures the same learners where nobody here wrote the environment: the 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games (183 levels, no instructions, a recorded human action count per level), played offline through the official toolkit and scored by the toolkit's own scorecard, which the tool cross-checks against its own tally and refuses to report if they disagree (that check caught this tool's first error: a level reset is counted as an action). A second check asks whether the adapter can reach what the games respond to: at each game's first state all 50 clicks the engine itself lists as valid, across the 13 games where it lists any, lead to an outcome that one of the adapter's one-per-region click targets also reaches. Result at 2, 5, 20 and 100 times the human action count: uniform random play 0.127 to 0.147 on average (humans = 100), the existing first-contact learner environment_learning_v1 0.000 to 0.0015, i.e. at or below random at every budget, completing at most 2 of 183 levels. It also adds systematic_exploration_v1, a deterministic frontier explorer that never pays twice for the same experiment and shares the transfer_learning_v1 store. On the five families constructed in this tree it reaches the goal with 4.26 times fewer act calls than the existing learner (5.52 with an effect prior); on the public games it completes at most 5 of 183 levels, and that only at 100 times the human action count. So a better explorer over the same state table is a real saving on small enumerable problems and is not what is missing. The measurement is an audit and a falsifier, not a target: no score is chased and no capability is claimed. SECOND HALF OF THE SAME CLAIM, ADDED 2026-11-11: the owner also asked whether doing a thing once means it is learned for good. That was measured on the 130 MiniWoB++ web task pages (Farama-Foundation, MIT, pages nobody here wrote), loaded into a headless DOM with a virtual clock, element-level actions, the page's own reward as the only judge. Per task the machine finds ONE success by itself on one instance (systematic exploration, no model), the success must replay on a fresh page, and each arm then gets ONE try on each of 20 instances it has not seen. Of 130 pages 110 run and repeat here and 61 yield a first success within 600 actions. Tasks solved on at least 18 of 20 unseen instances, counting only tasks where replaying the demonstration is not already enough: replay 0, random 0, the repository's own demonstration-to-skill compiler as it is 4, a new version-space learner from the one success 15, the same after three practice instances 18 (held-out three quarters of the tasks only: compiler 2, version space 11, with practice 12). A control that denies the skill the instance's own instruction shows which of those successes rest on reading it: 15 of 15 stop working without it. So one success becomes a skill on a minority of tasks, and which minority is decided by what the learner can describe, not by having done it once. Not a MiniWoB++ leaderboard entry (no browser, no pixels); producer-run; zero credit claimed. THEN THE PER-TASK FAILURES WERE READ, which ends the held-out status of every task for anything measured afterwards. The largest class among demonstrated-but-unlearned tasks was one missing relation: the control that sits in the same row or card as the thing the instruction names. That relation (nearest in the page tree to an element named by the instruction) and one binding (an element named by its kind) were added to the learner and the whole measurement was rerun: one success now gives 17 tasks (was 15), with three practice instances 19 (was 18); the other arms are unchanged. These second numbers are on tasks the producer had inspected; the first run, recorded before, is the only held-out evidence. THIRD RUN, 2026-11-11, IN A REAL BROWSER: the same measurement was moved from the headless DOM into headless Chromium (real layout, a click is a mouse press at the element's box, typing is key events, every episode a freshly opened page), and three things came out of it. (1) AN ERROR IN THE FIRST TWO RUNS: they counted any positive reward as success, and some pages pay part of the reward for part of the task. Success now means the page's full reward; episodes paid in part are counted apart. find-greatest, use-colorwheel and use-colorwheel-2, counted in V1 and V2 as solved by replay, were not. (2) 129 of 130 pages run and repeat (110 before). The first success is now searched for in an order read off the instruction (what it quotes is typed first, what it names is pressed first, every action is still tried); the order was written by the producer after reading pages and tried on about 18 of these tasks, so it is a prior put in by hand, not something learned. A first success is found on 69 pages at a median of 5 actions; on 59 it is not (on 21 of them everything that can be done was tried: the needed action kinds - drag, hover, a point, keys, waiting - do not exist here; 38 ran out of the 600-action budget). Replay is enough on 10. Where it is not: random 0, the existing compiler 6, the version-space learner from one success 19, the same denied the instruction 0, with three practice instances 24. Solved on at least 18 of 20 unseen instances in all: 29 of 130 from one success or replay, 34 of 130 with practice. Five tasks counted as solved in V2 are not in V3 (three for the reward error; use-spinner and form-sequence-3 because the first success found in the browser is a different one and generalises worse) and nine are solved in V3 that were not in V2. No task is held out any more. Half of the tasks (65) were run twice by two builds and every outcome was identical. (3) ONE MEMORY: the 127 programs kept from 69 tasks were put into a single library and one agent, never told which task a page belongs to, was scored on all 130 tasks: 36 solved (34 when each task is handed its own skill; none lost), and with everything learned on the task itself removed - first sight of the task - 24 solved, 3 of them the same page with and without a delay. Not one of the 61 tasks without a first success of their own was done at first sight: transfer reaches relatives of what was learned and no further. A first version of the library ranked programs by what differs only, and a program whose slot swallows its whole instruction then answered for every page; the ranking now also counts shared fixed words. Scratch, not in the digests: ten practice instances instead of three on ten near-miss tasks moved one over the line and made five slightly worse, so more tries do not repair what the description language cannot say. A crash was found and fixed on the way: leaving a step out of a found route shifted later element numbers and a plan naming an element that was not on the page was accepted; a replayed plan must now be doable step by step, and an error in one task is recorded against that task instead of ending the run. FOURTH RUN, 2026-11-11: the learner's language was extended and the measurement repeated with nothing else changed (on all 130 tasks the stage, the first success and its search cost are identical to run 3, and so is every outcome of the three arms the learner has no part in). Four additions, each read off recorded successes: a run of presses through exactly the elements of one kind that the instruction mentions becomes one step that serves any number of them; a press after which the next target first appeared is remembered as made to bring it out, and where the target is missing, elements of the same kind are pressed, each once and at most twelve, until it appears; an element's text may start or end with a quoted piece; typed text may be copied from an element found through the instruction. The producer wrote these after reading, instance by instance, where the run-3 skills stopped on the scored instances, so the counts there (29 to 39 tasks at or above 90 percent from one success, 34 to 44 with three practice instances) are too high. Both sets of kept skills were therefore scored on 20 further instances per task that nobody had looked at: 26 to 34 from one success and 30 to 38 with practice, of 130; successes 792 to 939 and 908 to 1021 of 1380. Eight tasks are newly learned there (the three checkbox tasks, the two collapsible-2 tasks, click-tab-2, click-tab-2-hard with practice or click-scroll-list from one success, read-table); the two autocomplete tasks looked learned on the read instances and are not, and with practice they are worse than before (13 of 20 against 17): the page asks in two ways, practice showed one, and a program good enough to pass practice by itself never gets sent to learn the other. The fresh instances also exposed a fault of the instrument that every earlier run has: a press lands on the centre of the element's box even where another element covers that point, so on pages that put two buttons at random places the right choice sometimes presses the wrong button (three of the simplest tasks drop from 19 to 16 of 20). It is not fixed in this run. Of 3510 actions taken while being scored, 175 were presses made only to look. Denied the instruction, the new skills solve 0 of the tasks where replay is not enough. ONE MEMORY with the new skills, on the read instances only: one agent holding all 111 programs and never told the task, 36 to 46 tasks at or above 90 percent of 130; at first sight of a task, with everything learned on it removed, 24 to 33; still none of the tasks without a first success of their own. Not done: the one-memory measurement on fresh instances; the question whether the order of presses matters was never put to a real page; nobody else has run any of this. What is left, counted on the scored instances: 61 tasks without a usable first success (21 because the actions they need - drag, hover, keys, a press at a point, waiting - do not exist here, 36 because the search ran out of budget, 4 for other reasons) and 25 with a first success and no skill that reaches 90 percent: they need what a person sees (colour, shape, size), or arithmetic, comparison and counting, or knowledge that is not on the page.

agent_orientation.earlier_routes_exhausted_reason: REUSE was done first and measured: the existing learners and causal_trace_to_skill_compiler_v1 were run unchanged through adapters, and the compiler solved 4 tasks where replay is not enough. Its generalisation is one rule (a literal shared by instruction and step becomes a parameter); page content it cannot tie to the instruction stays a constant, an instruction it cannot parse is refused, and its executor submits HTTP forms and cannot act on a live page. ADAPT of that 2033-line module was rejected: other organs call it and its held-out gate is built around file, SQLite and HTTP effects. finite_identifiability filters a hypothesis set it is handed and does not generate one; universal_parameterized_skill_candidate_v1 generalises scalar leaves of episodes with identical skeletons; neither describes which element on a page was acted on. COMPOSE covers the measurement (explorer plus adapters). What no existing module does is enumerate the descriptions of an acted-on element and strike out those a later success contradicts; that is the one new primitive, demonstration_version_space_v1.
